Downloading the functions that can read the data
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(ggfortify)
```


reading in the CSV files
*unos data set must be added to users own data-raw folder 
```{r}
unos <- readRDS("../data-raw/unos-ltx-art.rds")


us_zips<- read_csv(
  "../data/us-zips.csv",
  col_types = cols(
    .default = col_guess(),
    zip_code = col_character(),
    county_fips = col_character()
  )
)
```

looking at the names of the columns of each data set to see how to match them 
```{r}
names(unos)
names(us_zips)
```

Combining the UNOS dataset with the zip code data set from GitHub
```{r}
unos <- unos %>%
  mutate(ZIP = sprintf("%05d", as.integer(PERM_ZIP_TRR)))

merged_data <- unos %>%
  left_join(
    us_zips,
    by = c("PERM_ZIP_TRR" = "zip_code")
  )
```

Making sure the merged data carried the same number of rows so we didn't loose any data
```{r}
nrow(unos)
nrow(merged_data)
```

checks how many observations successfully received a county FIPS code after merging your ZIP code datasets
```{r}
# Check how many observations successfully matched to a county FIPS code
sum(!is.na(merged_data$county_fips))

# Check how many observations are missing a county FIPS code after merging
sum(is.na(merged_data$county_fips))
```

Calculates the percentage of observations that successfully received a county FIPS code after merging the datasets
```{r}
mean(!is.na(merged_data$county_fips)) * 100
```

creates a new dataset containing only the observations that are missing a county FIPS code after merging
```{r}
missing_zips <- merged_data %>%
  filter(is.na(county_fips))
missing_zips
```

check whether the original ZIP code reference dataset contains missing county FIPS values and examine the states associated with unmatched observations
```{r}
sum(is.na(us_zips$county_fips))
missing_zips %>%
  count(state, sort = TRUE)
```
261 observations with missing state information in your missing_zips dataset.

Identifies the unique ZIP codes that failed to match during the merge and checks whether those ZIP codes exist in the reference dataset (us_zips)
```{r}
unmatched_zips <- merged_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(ZIP), is.na(county_fips)) %>%
  distinct(ZIP)

unmatched_zips %>%
  mutate(
    exists_in_us_zips = ZIP %in% us_zips$zip_code
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

converts incorrectly formatted missing ZIP codes into actual missing values, reruns the merge, and identifies ZIP codes that still fail to match the reference dataset
```{r}

# Convert "000NA" values back into actual missing values (NA)
unos <- unos %>%
  mutate(ZIP = na_if(ZIP, "000NA"))

# Rerun the merge using the corrected ZIP codes
merged_data <- unos %>%
  left_join(us_zips, by = c("ZIP" = "zip_code"))
```
We get 33 rows which means we took care of the ones with no zip codes but still have to solve the issue of missing data. 

checks whether the previously unmatched ZIP codes have an exact match in the ZIP code reference dataset
```{r}
unmatched_zips %>%
  mutate(
    exact_match = ZIP %in% us_zips$zip_code
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```
The 33 that we identified are  marked as not found in the us_zips data set. 

Trying to make sure they are not in the data set rather than being ignored for some reason 
```{r}
"93596" %in% unos$ZIP
"93596" %in% us_zips$zip_code
```

```{r}
names(unos)
```

Cleaning the data again to  omit the participants with missing zipcodes 
```{r}
unos_clean <- unos %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(PERM_ZIP_TRR),
    !PERM_ZIP_TRR %in% c("000NA", "NA", "")
  )
unos_clean
```
```{r}
nrow(unos)
nrow(unos_clean)
```

Seeing how many participants we have after omitting the ones without zip codes 
```{r}
merge_data_without_missing <- unos_clean %>% 
  left_join(us_zips, by = c("PERM_ZIP_TRR" = "zip_code"))
nrow(merge_data_without_missing)
```

```{r}
# Number of distinct unmatched ZIP codes
misaligned_zipcodes <- merge_data_without_missing %>%
  filter(is.na(county_fips)) %>%
  summarise(n_distinct(PERM_ZIP_TRR))
misaligned_zipcodes
```
Lists out the zip codes that we are missing 
```{r}
missing_zips <- merge_data_without_missing %>%
  filter(is.na(county_fips)) %>%
  select(PERM_ZIP_TRR)

missing_zips
```

Filtering out all of the inactive and PO boxes that don't match with the downloaded zip code data set 
```{r}
offical_cleaned_data <- merge_data_without_missing %>%
  filter(!PERM_ZIP_TRR %in% missing_zips$PERM_ZIP_TRR)

#verifying that 33 of them were removed 
nrow(merge_data_without_missing) - nrow(offical_cleaned_data)

names(offical_cleaned_data)
```

Creating data set with Woodard and UNOS data
```{r}
woodardGEOID<- read.csv("../data/woodardZIPmerge.csv")

UNOSxWoodard <- offical_cleaned_data %>%
  left_join(woodardGEOID, by = c("county" = "COUNTY.NAME..SHORT."), relationship = "many-to-many")
  
UNOSxWood.clean<- UNOSxWoodard %>% select(-latitude, -longitude, -timezone, -metro_area, -median_household_income, -median_age, -households, - avg_household_size, - bachelors_or_higher_pct, -median_home_value, -median_gross_rent, -poverty_rate_pct, -unemployment_rate_pct, -primary_language, -ANSICODE,-ALAND, -AWATER, -ALAND_SQMI, -AWATER_SQMI, -INTPTLAT, -INTPTLONG)
 
```

Unos/Woodard Kruskal-Wallis Test
```{r}
Wood.KW <- kruskal.test(COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX ~ WOODARD.NATION.NAME, data = UNOSxWood.clean)

Wood.KW

ggplot(UNOSxWood.clean,
       aes(x = WOODARD.NATION.NAME,
           y = COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Post-Transplant Mortality by Woodard Nation",
    x = "Woodard Nation",
    y = "Composite Death"
  )

```
UNOS/UNOS Regionalization Kruskal-Wallis Test
```{r}
Region.KW <- kruskal.test(COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX ~ REGION, data = UNOSxWood.clean)

Region.KW


ggplot(UNOSxWood.clean,
       aes(x = REGION,
           y = COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "salmon", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Post-Transplant Mortality by Woodard Nation",
    x = "UNOS Region",
    y = "Composite Death DPTX"
  ) 

```

Creating a column connecting the 9 census divisions to their respective state

```{r}
UNOSxWood.clean <- UNOSxWood.clean %>%
  mutate(
    Census_Division = as.character(state.division[match(state, state.abb)])
  )

table(UNOSxWood.clean$Census_Division, useNA = "ifany")

```
UNOS/Census Division Kruskal-Wallis Test
```{r}
Census.KW <- kruskal.test(COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX ~ Census_Division, data = UNOSxWood.clean)

Census.KW

ggplot(UNOSxWood.clean,
       aes(x = Census_Division,
           y = COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgreen", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Post-Transplant Mortality by Woodard Nation",
    x = "US Census Divison",
    y = "Composite Death DPTX"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

Kaplan Meier Analysis 

Definition of Status & Time
```{r}

UNOSxWood.clean$status <- ifelse(UNOSxWood.clean$COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX > UNOSxWood.clean$PX_STAT_DPTX | is.na(UNOSxWood.clean$COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX), 0,1)
 

UNOSxWood.clean$surv_time <- pmin(UNOSxWood.clean$PX_STAT_DPTX, UNOSxWood.clean$COMPOSITE_DEATH_DPTX, na.rm = TRUE)

```



Woodard Nations KM & Log-Rank Analysis for 1, 6 & 10 years

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}

Woodardkm <- survfit(
  Surv(
    time = surv_time,
    event = status
) ~ WOODARD.NATION.NAME, data = UNOSxWood.clean
)


summary(Woodardkm, times=365.2422*c(1,6,10))


Woodard_logrank <- survdiff(
  Surv(
    time = surv_time,
    event = status
) ~ WOODARD.NATION.NAME, data = UNOSxWood.clean
)

Woodard_logrank

Woodard_plot <- fortify(Woodardkm) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = time / 365.2422, y = surv)) +
  geom_step(aes(color = strata)) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_brewer(
    type = "qual", palette = "Paired",
    aesthetics = c("color", "fill"), name = ""
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(x = "Years since transplant", y = "Surviving percent (patients)")
print(Woodard_plot)

ggsave("Woodard-surv-km.pdf", width = unit(10, "in"), height = unit(8, "in"))
```
